causal_chain: A small bank of persistent user states can store separable preference modes without requiring session labels.
Conditioning a transport operator on the user's recent training-history items lets the model shift state emphasis toward the intent most relevant to the current scoring context.
Pairwise training then reinforces both which state should win for a positive item and how recent evidence should transport the state mixture away from negatives.
This should improve full-sort ranking when held-out positives align with one latent taste mode that would be diluted in single-embedding collaborative filters.
Users in ML-1M often express mixed tastes that are poorly summarized by one static user vector.
blind_projection.closest_parent: A recommender that models each user as a small set of persistent latent preference states and updates those states through pairwise event-conditioned memory transport will better capture mixed and shifting tastes than single-embedding models, yielding higher full-sort NDCG@10 under the same offline pairwise protocol.
blind_projection.competing_explanation: Any gain could come merely from increased parameter count or an extra nonlinear scorer rather than from multi-state memory transport itself.
discriminative_predictions: Ablating transport while keeping the same state bank should reduce performance more on users whose recent training interactions differ from their long-run average profile, indicating the benefit is not only static multi-intent capacity.

Compared with a matched single-state mechanism-off control, the proposed model should show larger improvements for users with longer and more genre-diverse training histories than for short, homogeneous histories.
The learned routing weights over user states should be sharper for positives than sampled negatives, whereas the mechanism-off control has no such state-selective separation.
expected_evidence: Internal diagnostics show non-collapsed usage of multiple states and nontrivial transport updates from recent-history context.
Qualification runs produce a measurable NDCG@10 delta versus the matched mechanism-off control under the frozen ML-1M protocol.
User-slice analysis by history diversity or recency-shift shows concentrated gains in mixed-taste users.
blind_projection.falsifier: If a matched single-state or no-transport control matches or exceeds the candidate on full-sort NDCG@10, or if the candidate collapses to effectively uniform state usage across users and items, the memory-transport mechanism is not supported.
blind_projection.high_change_justification: This proposal changes the core representation from one user embedding to a user-specific state set, changes the interaction structure by routing scores through state selection conditioned on candidate and recent history, and adds a custom transport capability that updates the scoring state from ordered training interactions. These are mechanism-level changes rather than tuning or shallow wrappers.
blind_projection.hypothesis: A candidate-local RecBole GeneralRecommender that represents each user as a small bank of persistent latent preference states and scores each item through recent-history-conditioned transport plus disagreement-aware state routing will improve ML-1M full-sort NDCG@10 over matched single-state collaborative filtering, because it can preserve multiple long-run tastes while shifting toward the intent most supported by the user's recent training interactions.
implementation_requirements: Build per-user ordered training histories from the frozen train split timestamps only; do not access validation or test interactions for state updates.
Compute candidate-item score by routing over transported user states with candidate-conditioned attention or softmax gating.
Generate a transport delta from recent-history context to update each user state before scoring.
Implement a candidate-local GeneralRecommender with pairwise BPR-style loss and full-sort prediction over all items.
Log diagnostics for state usage entropy, transport magnitude, and slice metrics by user history diversity.
Maintain K learnable user state embeddings plus item embeddings and a recent-history context encoder based on the last L training items.
Provide an executable mechanism-off variant in the same codebase that removes transport and state routing while preserving pairwise training and comparable parameter budget.
blind_projection.matched_control_requirement: Use a candidate-local matched control with the same optimizer, item embeddings, training loop, pairwise loss family, and approximately matched parameter count, but with a single user state and no recent-history-conditioned transport or candidate-conditioned state routing.
blind_projection.mechanism_change: Introduce a Multi-State Transported Preference Routing recommender: each user owns K persistent latent states; recent training-history items are encoded into a context vector; this context produces a transport update applied to the state bank; for each candidate item, a routing gate selects or mixes transported states based on state-item compatibility and state-context disagreement; the final score is the gated affinity between the candidate item and transported user states.
blind_projection.mechanism_off_definition: Mechanism-off is a matched single-state affinity model implemented in the same candidate-local class family: replace the user state bank with one user embedding, disable recent-history-conditioned transport, disable candidate-conditioned routing, and score by a direct user-item dot product under the same pairwise training and full-sort evaluation protocol.
blind_projection.minimal_testable_wedge: A two-condition qualification: (1) the proposed multi-state transported routing model and (2) a matched mechanism-off single-state no-transport control, both trained once under the frozen ML-1M protocol with identical data pipeline and comparable parameter budget.
blind_projection.research_question: Under the frozen ML-1M pairwise full-sort protocol, does adding recent-history-conditioned transport over a small bank of persistent user preference states improve ranking beyond a matched single-state collaborative filter?
blind_projection.resource_hypothesis: The candidate is feasible within the stated budget because ML-1M is small enough to cache ordered user histories in memory, the transport module can be implemented with lightweight MLP projections over recent-item averages, and full-sort scoring remains standard matrix multiplication plus a small routing step per user batch.
